subject: general
question: Who introduced the policy of Paramountcy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Hastings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lord Hastings, who was the Governor-General of India from 1813 to 1823, introduced a new policy of 'paramountcy'.
 
• By this policy, the Company claimed that its authority was paramount or supreme, hence its power was greater than that of Indian states.
 
• The chief instrument through which Lord Dalhousie implemented his policy of annexation was the ‘Doctrine of Lapse’.
 
 
• Under the Doctrine of Lapse, when the ruler of a protected state died without a natural heir, his/her state was not to pass to an adopted heir as sanctioned by the age-old tradition of the country.
 
• Lord Dalhousie came to India as the Governor-General in 1848.
 
• During Lord Canning's tenure “Doctrine of Lapse” was withdrawn.
 
 
 
• British Imperial policies between 1763 and 1776 were focused on using the colonies to raise revenue in ways that the colonists saw as unconstitutional.
 
 
• 
 
The majority of the colonists were extremely loyal to the crown and only became “reluctant revolutionists” when there was no other choice.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Dalhousie**

 
 
• The annexation of Awadh by Lord Dalhousie took place in the year 1856.
 
• Lord Dalhousie was the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856.
 
• The annexation was justified by Dalhousie under the pretext of misgovernment by the Nawab of Awadh.
 
• This event was one of the significant causes leading to the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• The policy of annexation was part of Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse, which aimed at expanding British territories in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Ripon** 
 
 
• The Hunter Commission of 1882 was presided by Sir William Hunter and was appointed by Lord Ripon, the then viceroy of India.
 
• The hunter commission was constituted on 3rd April 1882, after a request of the general council of education was made to Ripon. 
 
• Sir William Hunter was an Indian Civil Service officer and a member of the Executive Council of the Viceroy.
 
• The following were the main objectives :
 
 
• Consider different aspects of education in India, paying particular attention to primary education.
 
• Enquire into the execution of Wood’s Despatch of 1854 and suggest ways to improve outcomes of the same.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Lord Cornwallis​** 
 
 
• The police system was created by Lord Cornwallis. 
 
• The police commission was appointed by him in Kolkata.
 
• He relieved the Zamindars from police functions and established a regular police force in 1791. 
 
• Cornwallis established a system of circles or ‘thanas’ each headed by a ‘daroga’. 
 
• The authority of the daroga extended to village watchmen who performed the police duties in the villages. 
 
• The hereditary village police became ‘chowkidars’. 
 
• In the big cities, the old office of kotwal was, however, continued, and a daroga was appointed to each of the wards of a city. 
 
• The daroga system was extended to Madras in 1802. 
 
• The post of the district superintendent of police was created, and all the thanas were under the general supervision of the district judge. 
 
• In 1808, a Superintendent of Police was appointed for each division. 
 
• Later, the district collector was entrusted with the task of controlling the police force in the districts. 
 
• The main task of the police was to handle crime and prevent conspiracy against British rule.
